I think about this year like I did last year. I am old, 76, only farmed one year alone. Before that my son did most of it but now he went to work in the city so I follow what the neighbors tell me.

My land is 5.5 mu. Not much. Four mu I grow wheat in winter and maize in summer — same field, two crops, like everyone here. The other one and a half mu I keep in cotton. That was my wife's idea long ago, we always kept some cotton.

For wheat, I do what neighbor old Zhang does. When I plant in October I spread two bags of compound fertilizer per mu — the one with three 15s on the bag, 40 jin each bag I think, no, 50 jin. Two bags. Then in spring when the wheat turns green I put one bag of urea per mu. That's what he told me. I cannot read the bag but the shop man knows what I need. I water the wheat three times — before winter, green-up, and when it heads. The well is close so water is not too dear.

For maize after wheat, I do not plow, just push the seed in with the machine the neighbor hires. I put one bag compound when planting, then one bag urea when it is knee-high. Two sprays for the worm, the shop sells me the bottle. Water maybe twice if no rain.

Cotton is more trouble. More fertilizer, more spray. I put two bags compound and one bag urea. Spray five or six times because the bugs are bad. Water three times.

I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than lose the harvest. Fertilizer is money but empty grain bin is worse.
